problem: Move DIG from local framed stdio toward a real Qubes lab boundary without opening a network listener or broadening trust.

candidates.name: pinned-qrexec-policy-plus-local-secret
candidates.notes: Pin one source qube to one coordinator qube, deny all fallback, keep HMAC secret out of policy/service artifacts, preserve existing framed stdio protocol.

candidates.name: wildcard-qrexec-policy
candidates.notes: Simple but unnecessarily expands which qubes may invoke the coordinator service.

candidates.name: http-listener-between-qubes
candidates.notes: Adds network attack surface and duplicates security properties already provided by qrexec plus authenticated envelopes.

candidates.name: embed-worker-secret-in-service-or-policy
candidates.notes: Rejected: secrets would leak into deployment artifacts or repository history and rotation would be unsafe.

why: It preserves the existing no-listener stdio design, minimizes Qubes policy scope, keeps per-worker secrets provisioned locally with owner-only permissions, and has the smallest regression surface.
failuresAndLessons: A wildcard allow rule would undermine the worker identity boundary before HMAC verification and is unnecessary for the lab.
Secrets must never be committed into qrexec policy, service scripts, or repository fixtures.
Qrexec transport policy and application HMAC solve different layers: source/target authorization versus worker request authentication and replay fencing.
Real-Qube fault injection is still required before REAL-WORKER READY; generated artifacts alone are not deployment evidence.
safetyScope: Synthetic defensive orchestration only; no real financial transactions, stolen payment data, external exploitation, or weakened security controls.
